title: reference-impl v0.6.2 — leftover dogfood debt (merge=union for CHANGELOG)
problem: Three bugs from the v0.6 and v0.6.1 walker dogfoods remain unaddressed and continue to cost real time on every substantive Plan run. Bug #3 (cross-browser system deps): install.sh calls npx playwright install chromium webkit firefox unconditionally but its system-deps step only covers webkit, not firefox; CLV-28 of the v0.6 dogfood spent ~30 min hand-extracting .deb files for firefox before the human ran sudo apt-get install. Bug #12 (Documenter CHANGELOG conflict): when a Plan has multiple parallel tasks each Documenter writes a ## [Unreleased] entry to reference-impl/CHANGELOG.md; sibling branches collide on the same lines during walker rebase or merge, requiring manual git checkout --ours CHANGELOG.md resolution (CLV-34 first-merge and CLV-36 second-merge of the v0.6.1 dogfood both hit this). Bug #13 (Session B CWD drift): on the v0.6.1 CLV-36 run, Session B's CWD silently drifted into a standard/ subdirectory during normal operation; subsequent git ls-tree HEAD calls returned paths without the reference-impl/ prefix, costing ~30 min of confused diff inspection before recovery. None of these have mitigations in v0.6.1 (HEAD 580bec9). This RFC supersedes the abandoned CLV-40, which proposed an extensions-vocabulary-based custodian (clv.version-bump-custodian + clv.changelog-suppressed) for bug #12 — that approach was rejected at Plan-review time as over-engineered relative to a one-line git-native fix.
solution:
Three focused bug fixes ship as @cloverleaf/reference-impl@0.6.2 with no Standard changes (stays at 0.4.1) and no new vocabulary, agents, or external API surface. The three fixes have no shared-file overlap and run as fully parallel root tasks under a release-prep join sink.

Bug #1 — Cross-browser system deps (install.sh): The CLV-41 spike (still valid, carried over from CLV-40) confirmed (a) install.sh already runs npx playwright install chromium webkit firefox unconditionally; the gap is only install-deps, (b) on non-Linux platforms playwright's installer prints a platform-warning and exits 0 with no system changes — no extra bash guard needed, (c) the config-driven approach is blocked by a bootstrap problem (consumer config is unavailable at install time). install.sh gains an explicit --with-cross-browser CLI flag parsed from "$@" at the top. When present on Linux, the script replaces the existing npx playwright install-deps webkit-only call with npx playwright install-deps webkit firefox. When absent on Linux, the existing install-deps webkit behavior is preserved. On non-Linux the install-deps call is a playwright-level no-op regardless. When absent the script prints: "(Pass --with-cross-browser to also install webkit/firefox system deps for cross-browser UI review.)". README documents the flag. A shell-mock regression test asserts the conditional invocation.

Bug #2 — Documenter CHANGELOG conflict (.gitattributes merge=union): Add the line `reference-impl/CHANGELOG.md merge=union` to the repo's .gitattributes (creating the file if absent). The merge=union driver is built into git: when two branches both modify the same lines, git includes both sides' lines instead of producing a conflict. For an append-only ## [Unreleased] section where each Documenter adds per-task ### Added/### Changed/### Fixed bullets at the time of doc commit, this is exactly the right semantic — every per-task entry survives, no manual rebase, the file is never marked conflicted. Documenter's contract is unchanged (no prompt edits, no task-level metadata, no Plan-agent coordination). The release-prep custodian (T4) still owns the ## [Unreleased] → ## 0.6.2 rename, the date stamp, and final ordering / de-duplication. Per-task richness is preserved — Discovery agents and human readers depend on detailed per-fix CHANGELOG entries. No fallback; merge=union is a built-in git driver, not a third-party dependency. Tradeoff: merge=union may interleave bullets in non-deterministic order when multiple branches merge in close succession; the custodian's release-prep pass normalizes ordering at version-rename time. A regression test verifies that two simulated branches each adding distinct ## [Unreleased] bullets merge cleanly with both bullets present and no conflict markers.

Bug #3 — Session B CWD drift: Both sub-options are applied. Walker-side: reference-impl/skills/cloverleaf-run-plan/SKILL.md embeds the absolute WORKTREE_ROOT path in the Session B scenario brief, with an explicit instruction that Session B's first preflight step must execute cd "$WORKTREE_ROOT" before any git command. Prompt-side: all five agent prompts (implementer.md, documenter.md, reviewer.md, ui-reviewer.md, qa.md) gain cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" as their first executable preflight line, anchoring each agent to the worktree root regardless of CWD drift source. With bug #2 no longer touching any agent prompt or SKILL.md, T3 has no shared-file overlap with T2.

DAG topology: Three parallel root tasks — (T1) install.sh cross-browser fix touching install.sh only; (T2) CHANGELOG merge=union touching .gitattributes (and a regression test under reference-impl/tests/) only; (T3) CWD drift fix touching SKILL.md and all five agent prompts — converge into (T4) a release-prep join-sink task that is the sole custodian of reference-impl/CHANGELOG.md (renames ## [Unreleased] to ## 0.6.2 with date, normalizes bullet order) and reference-impl/package.json (0.6.1 → 0.6.2). No shared-file edges among T1/T2/T3.
acceptance_criteria: install.sh parses --with-cross-browser from "$@" at the top of the script; when the flag is present on a Linux/apt-based platform, npx playwright install-deps webkit firefox is invoked (replacing the current unconditional install-deps webkit-only call).

install.sh without --with-cross-browser on Linux preserves the existing npx playwright install-deps webkit behavior and does not invoke install-deps firefox; the script prints an informational note: "(Pass --with-cross-browser to also install webkit/firefox system deps for cross-browser UI review.)".

install.sh with --with-cross-browser on non-Linux platforms does not fail — playwright handles non-apt platforms as a graceful no-op (warning + exit 0), so no additional bash platform guard is required.

A shell-mock regression test in reference-impl/tests/ (or reference-impl/scripts/) verifies that playwright install-deps webkit firefox is invoked when --with-cross-browser is present and that only install-deps webkit (not install-deps firefox) is invoked when the flag is absent.
The repo .gitattributes contains the line: reference-impl/CHANGELOG.md merge=union (file created if absent).

A regression test verifies that two simulated branches each adding distinct ## [Unreleased] bullets to reference-impl/CHANGELOG.md merge cleanly with merge=union: both bullets are present in the merge result, the file is not marked conflicted, and no manual resolution is needed.

reference-impl/prompts/documenter.md is unchanged in its CHANGELOG behavior — it still writes per-task ## [Unreleased] entries with appropriate ### Added / ### Changed / ### Fixed subheadings at the time of the doc commit.

reference-impl/skills/cloverleaf-run-plan/SKILL.md embeds the absolute WORKTREE_ROOT path in the Session B scenario brief with an explicit instruction to cd "$WORKTREE_ROOT" as the first preflight step.

All five agent prompts (reference-impl/prompts/implementer.md, documenter.md, reviewer.md, ui-reviewer.md, qa.md) include cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" (or an equivalent absolute anchor) as the first executable preflight step.

The v0.6.2 delivery run of this RFC's Plan completes without any manual git checkout --ours CHANGELOG.md rebase resolution — enforced structurally by .gitattributes merge=union, not by a Plan custodian convention.

reference-impl/CHANGELOG.md contains a ## 0.6.2 section (renamed from ## [Unreleased] by the release-prep custodian) listing all three bug fixes: cross-browser system deps (#3 from v0.6 dogfood), Documenter CHANGELOG conflict (#12 from v0.6.1 dogfood), and Session B CWD drift (#13 from v0.6.1 dogfood).
@cloverleaf/standard version remains at 0.4.1 and its package.json is not modified.
Tag reference-impl-v0.6.2 is created, a GitHub Release is published with a summary of the three fixes, and npm publish is executed for @cloverleaf/reference-impl@0.6.2.
out_of_scope: Dogfood debt #5 — chrome-devtools MCP single-profile contention across parallel walker sessions. Claw-drive architecture; not a reference-impl change.
Dogfood debt #8 — DAG-edge inference from shared-file modification overlap. Deferred to v0.7 design; the v0.6.2 Plan itself relies on file-overlap awareness encoded directly in this RFC.
The unified /cloverleaf-flow orchestrator that fuses Discovery and Delivery. Deferred to v0.7 scope.
Changes to @cloverleaf/standard schemas, contracts, or conformance harness. The Standard stays at 0.4.1 and its package.json is not touched.
New tracks, agents, or skills beyond the three in-scope bug fixes.
API changes to the walker skill: skill name, invocation arguments, and exit behavior are unchanged; only internal SKILL.md prose, agent prompt files, install.sh, and .gitattributes change.
Retroactively amending the v0.6.1 CHANGELOG or re-running v0.6.1 release branches. Those conflicts are already resolved on main via --ours and the v0.6.1 section is correct.

An extensions-vocabulary-based Documenter custodian (clv.version-bump-custodian + clv.changelog-suppressed). This was the approach in the abandoned CLV-40 RFC; it was rejected as over-engineered relative to the git-native one-line .gitattributes merge=union solution adopted here. Spike CLV-42's findings remain on disk as a research artifact.
